text:
alex: Heads-up — saw multiple failed pods when we tried to scale the new eu-west-1 A100 node pool. Terraform apply succeeded but kubelet failed CNI setup repeatedly.

maria: Any errors in kubelet logs? Sounds like CNI MTU mismatch from previous overlay changes.

alex: Logs show `flannel: interface down` and `network: CNI returned non-zero exit status`. Packet capture shows jumbo frames being dropped. MTU on the host is 9000 but CNI defaulted to 1500 after the cluster-image upgrade.

jing: Oof. That's the commit where we changed calico helm values to use `overlay: vxlan` and left MTU implicit. I've seen this break bigger kernels with GPU drivers because of fragmentation.

tom: Is this specific to GPU nodepool? Why are GPUs impacted more than CPU nodes?

alex: GPUs stream huge bundles (checkpoint pulls, model artifacts) during startup; the fragmentation overwhelms the NVMe driver path and kubelet times out mounting csidrivers. CPU nodes just retry slower — GPU pods hit readiness probes and get killed.

maria: Quick mitigation: roll back calico mtu to 9000 for eu-west-1 overlay and drain+recreate the pool OR set `hostNetwork: true` for the node init DaemonSet that pulls artifacts (temporary). Which is less risky?

jing: Rollback calico MTU in values via Helm is safer long-term. We can patch the nodepool taint to prevent production queues (label) from landing during the window.

alex: I'll open a terraform plan to change the helm_release values and update nodepool annotation to `redwood.io/boot-drain=true` so we can auto-provision but keep schedulable=false until healthy.

tom: If you go the terraform route, also update the autoscaler configmap to bump `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 15m. Otherwise it might evict still-provisioning GPU pods.

alex: Good catch — autoscaler currently 5m. I'll change to 15m in the helm chart values for cluster-autoscaler.

maria: Also let's add `--scan-interval=30s` and annotate GPU pools with `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled=true` explicitly. We've seen implicit detection miss them on node labels.

alex: Pushing a quick terraform snippet for the helm release override I'm going to apply:
text2:
jing: That looks right. Add a `lifecycle` block on the nodepool resource to force recreate so taints/labels apply cleanly.

alex: Also including a small helm values patch for cluster-autoscaler: 
```yaml
replicaCount: 2
extraArgs:
  scale-down-unneeded-time: 15m
  scan-interval: 30s
nodeSelector:
  redwood-infra/gpu: "true"
metrics:
  enabled: true
```

tom: Cost question — if we recreate the pool as on-demand to stabilize, we'll pay a premium for 2-4 hours. Should we convert to spot after it's healthy?

maria: Yes: plan to provision as on-demand for the rollout window, validate, then switch to spot with a small reserved buffer (1-2 nodes) for critical queues. Reservation is cheaper if steady-state.

alex: I'll run `terraform plan` then apply against the eu-west workspace after a short maintenance window. Will ping infra-scheduler and the SRE rotation.

ci-bot: deploy-checklist: impact: node reboots, networking restart; estimated downtime for affected GPU pods: 10-20m.

jing: After MTU fix we should add an automation test in our infra CI that creates a small GPU nodepool and verifies artifact pulls and kubelet readiness within 7m. Catches regressions.

tom: Agree. Also add an alert: `kubelet.startup.failures > 5` on new nodes in 10m.

alex: Applying changes in ~30m. I'll post the terraform plan output and link to the PR here. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — if anyone is around when you apply, please watch the autoscaler and kubelet logs for errors.

alex: Plan posted: https://git.redwood.dev/r/infra/helm/+/PR-482 (includes helm values and autoscaler bump).

ci-bot: plan-ok: no unexpected drift for non-targeted resources.

jing: Noted — we'll follow with a CI job to create a smoke pool once this lands.
notes: No title field included per agents.md rules. Thread focuses on MTU-related GPU node provisioning failures, terraform/helm remediation, autoscaler config, and cost/spot strategy.
